recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-26835 unless a future work-group decision intentionally changes group-level visibility or editability inheritance.
issue_request: FHIR-26835 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Questionnaire and asked whether Questionnaire.item.readOnly=true on an item of type group makes sub-items read-only, and whether a descendant can override that with readOnly=false.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites commit 4b602199a770c77983f89646ed0ee358157e4efb, which added the Questionnaire notes Group properties section explaining that group readOnly, disabled enableWhen, and hidden-style controls affect descendants and that conflicting descendant settings may be reported as errors or warnings.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. Later same-change-family issue FHIR-29311 clarified that readOnly on a question affects only that question's own answer and not descendant questions; FHIR-29311 is already represented on the combined branch. Confluence SDC minutes for 2020-05-21 record the FHIR-26835 vote, and a 2025 Zulip thread confirms the current group readOnly interpretation.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the active Questionnaire narrative and StructureDefinition comments already implement the seed decision when read with later FHIR-29311 context.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Questionnaire clarification established that group readOnly affects descendants while question readOnly affects only the question's own answer; it is already represented on the combined branch.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 clarification asking whether Questionnaire group readOnly applies to descendants and can be overridden by descendant readOnly=false.
evidence_items.learned: The accepted decision says group-level visibility and editability controls apply to descendants and conflicting descendant declarations do not override the ancestor setting.

evidence_items.summary: The active Questionnaire notes include a Group properties section stating that group readOnly, disabled enableWhen, and hidden-style controls apply to descendants and child conflicts do not override the group.
evidence_items.learned: The relevant narrative source is in current build scope and already carries the seed clarification.

evidence_items.summary: Questionnaire.item.enableWhen says disabled items disable descendants, and Questionnaire.item.readOnly says group readOnly makes all items beneath the group read-only while question readOnly does not affect descendant questions.
evidence_items.learned: The StructureDefinition comments remain consistent with FHIR-26835 when read together with the later FHIR-29311 clarification for non-group questions.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-26835 application commit added the Questionnaire group-properties guidance to source/questionnaire/questionnaire-notes.xml.
evidence_items.learned: The seed issue has an explicit application in source history and that guidance is still present.

evidence_items.summary: Minutes record the FHIR-26835 vote as agreement that enableWhen, hidden, and read-only should apply to all subitems.
evidence_items.learned: Work-group meeting evidence supports the Jira decision and current group-properties text.

evidence_items.summary: In 2025, Lloyd McKenzie pointed to the Questionnaire group section and confirmed that readOnly groups make all descendants read-only even if children explicitly say readOnly=false.
evidence_items.learned: Later community discussion reinforces the current interpretation and reveals no conflict requiring a source change.
